rationale: R7_AUDIT_FLEET. R7 is the ambiguity rule: an endpoint must NAME A REAL DECLARATION, not a placeholder. `validation/m60/ledger.json` states the consequence — 'a literal in a name-bearing field becomes a symbol (or an edge endpoint) that does not exist in the source' — and its ENFORCED half is a SOURCE-level census whose marker is the literal `unknown`, so `global` was invisible to it. Measured over 110 ripgrep `.rs` files through the production entry, 1,280 of 29,660 edges named the literal `global` on their SOURCE. These pins are the four shapes that produced them, written before the analyzer change so they are expectations rather than a transcript. (1) A file-scope `static`/`const` OWNS its initializer: the `Choice { .. }` literals and the `Vec::new`/`acc.push` calls are attributed to `CHOICES` and `ALIASES`, which are real declarations this file writes. Before the change every one of them was attributed to `global`. (2) A `let` inside a closure inside that initializer binds LOCALLY and declares nothing outside its body (M11.11), so `acc` publishes no symbol. This is the regression guard for a defect the fix EXPOSED: M11.11's boundary tested only the immediate parent for Function|Method, so the moment a `static` became an owner, `let mut acc` began publishing a Variable owned by ALIASES. Found by diffing the 5,150-symbol inventory file by file, not by reading. (3) A file-scope `macro_invocation` has no owning declaration, so R7's own sentence governs — 'the honest state is ABSENCE' — and the `bodyprobe!` edge is FORBIDDEN rather than published under a fake owner. Its argument is an opaque `token_tree`, which is why the body contributes nothing at all: that is the grammar's statement, not a gap in this fixture. (4) A two-segment path rooted at a Rust PATH KEYWORD keeps the whole written path: `super`, `crate` and `self` are relative anchors, not crates and not modules, so leaf-dropping onto one published a keyword (69 rows on the lane corpus: 36 `super`, 33 `crate`). The bare roots are FORBIDDEN so the leaf-drop cannot creep back. (5) A `pub` item's export names the FILE as its source — `(file)` with `metadata.fileLevel: true`, the M60/#910 contract parallel-indexer.ts:3481 acts on. Not cosmetic: `global` is not on the store's SYMBOL_NAME_DENYLIST, so the store wrote `source_external = "global"`, which no reader can join on, and both of bb_graph's file-level queries were unreachable for every Rust imports/exports row. (6) The global forbid below is the rule stated once, so a re-introduced `global` fallback anywhere in this file fails even if every pin above still matched. (7) The last shape is the one the fixture could not express until the grammar was read: a macro invocation's ARGUMENT is an opaque `token_tree` to tree-sitter-rust, so the closure inside `rgtest!(..)` does not exist in the tree as a closure, a call or a field access — only `identifier` and `token_tree` nodes. The DFS descends into them anyway, and every name the macro was handed was read as if this file evaluated it (205 identifier reads in `tests/feature.rs` alone, 36 surviving the (source,target) dedupe as published `uses` edges sourced at the `global` fallback). A macro may discard or never expand its input, so `uses -> SHERLOCK_MARKER` is a claim the source does not make. RUST-D2 already declared a macro's BODY opaque; this extends the same principle to its ARGUMENT, and the two forbids below are the gate.
